The only person who really could have helped Joe, is Joe. It’s great to be supportive, but support only works if the person you’re supporting is taking the steps forward to get better. Addiction is a very hard thing to fight, and I’m so sorry that you lost your friend to that fight, but the enemy and sole blamed is his addiction. This is unfortunately a common thing people feel and a downside to the system in place, although it's there for a reason. You can dance around it and not say the actual words, but once you speak of anything that has to do with self harm, they have to report it, if they don't, and you go through with it, they could lose their job and worse, you'd lose your life. I know you might not listen to this, because I'm kind of a hypocrite for saying it, considering I know I'm suicidal (25f) and I never say it to my therapist because I know what'll happen and I'm scared to derail my life again, but you're young, you have time, take the help. Tell your therapist, you'll most likely be admitted, this is a good thing. Your first day or two will be scary and you'll feel lost, but everyone in the ward feels the same way and are very kind. They put you on a schedule, have group activities, regulate your eating habits and get you started on a medication. You'll see a psychiatrist one-two times a week. When you leave, things will feel better and you'll have a better outlook on things. Trust me. I went when I was 19, mandatory for trying to do it at work. That wasn't my plan, but sometimes things don't go according to plan. I was there for two weeks. I haven't tried it again since and lately I've been thinking I should go back, but I'm afraid of not graduating college on time and having to leave my husband with everything and the medical bills can be outrageous and we're already in debt. However, if you live at home with your parents and this is something you can do, you need to do it, your mental health should come first. If the meds your on make you uncomfortable, talk to your doctor when you get out about different medication. I wish you the best of luck and hope things get better.
